content: Sulfadiazine is a sulfa-based antibiotic that works by eliminating bacteria responsible for causing infections, particularly urinary tract infections. It is important to note that antibiotics like sulfadiazine are ineffective against viral infections such as colds or the flu. This medication may also be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Sulfadiazine is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically administered three to six times daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take sulfadiazine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. The tablets should be taken with a full glass of water. Continue taking sulfadiazine even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before starting sulfadiazine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to sulfadiazine, other sulfa drugs, diuretics (water pills), oral diabetes medications, or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin (Coumadin), diabetes medications, diuretics, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had liver or kidney disease, asthma, severe allergies, or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, which is an inherited blood disorder. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking sulfadiazine, contact your doctor immediately. Additionally, avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and wear protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as sulfadiazine may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. While taking sulfadiazine, you should drink plenty of fluids and take the medication on an empty stomach. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Sulfadiazine may cause side effects. Mild side effects include diarrhea, upset stomach, loss of appetite, and dizziness. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention and include rash or skin changes, sore throat, fever, headache, joint or muscle aches, yellowing of the skin or eyes, swelling of the lips or tongue, difficulty swallowing, fatigue, weakness, blood in the urine, difficulty breathing, unusual bleeding or bruising, and ringing in the ears. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store sulfadiazine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still experience symptoms of infection after completing the course of sulfadiazine, contact your doctor.
